==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:sours}} From {{inh|en|enm|sours}}, from {{der|en|fro|sorse||rise, beginning, spring, source}}, from {{m|fro|sors}}, past participle of {{m|fro|sordre}}, {{m|fro|sourdre}}, from {{der|en|la|surgō||to rise}}, which is composed of {{prefix|la|sub|regō|t1=up from below|t2=lead, rule|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃réǵeti||to straighten; right}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}. {{dbt|en|surge}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|horse-hoarse}} ** {{IPA|en|/sɔːs/|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/soːs/|a=SSB,AU,NZ}} *** {{audio|en|En-uk-source.ogg|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|/soɹs/|a=GenAm,Canada}} *** {{audio|en|en-us-source.ogg|a=US}} * {{a|en|non-horse-hoarse}} ** {{IPA|en|/soɾs/|a=Scotland}} ** {{IPA|en|/soːs/|a=Manchester}} ** {{IPA|en|/soəs/|a=Eastern New England}} ** {{IPA|en|/sɔəs/|a=19th century <>, obsolete}} * {{i|obsolete}} {{IPA|en|/suːɹs/|/sʊɹs/}}{{R:Jespersen MEGoHP|I|13.36|368}} * {{homophones|en|sauce|aa=non-rhotic,horse-hoarse}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)s|s=1}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # The [[person]], [[place]]{{,}} or [[thing]] from which something (information, goods, etc.) [[come]]s or is [[acquire]]d. #: {{syn|en|[[fund]] (formal)|storehouse}} #: {{ux|en|The accused refused to reveal the '''source''' of the illegal drugs she was selling.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Venezuela's Islands in Time|author=Uwe George|page=544 |text=To this day I do not know the '''source''' of the terrible screams that night in the labyrinth. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for new '''sources''' of return.}} # [[spring|Spring]]; [[fountainhead]]; [[wellhead]]; any collection of water on or under the surface of the ground in which a stream originates. #: {{ux|en|The main '''sources''' of the Euphrates River are the Karasu and Murat Rivers.}} #* {{quote-journal |en |date=3 July 1969 |origdate=28 May 1969 |original={{lang|zh|額爾齊斯河流域風貌}} |by={{lang|zh|念澄}} |title=A View of the O-erh-ch'i-ssu River Delta |journal=Translations on People's Republic of China |issue=59 |issueurl=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015030774064&seq=7 |publisher=w:United States Joint Publications Research Service |source=Hong Kong, [[w:Ta Kung Pao|Ta Kung Pao]], [https://archive.org/details/NPTKP19690528/page/n7/ p 8] |origlang=zh |oclc=2370938 |section=Economic |page=11 |pageurl=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015030774064&seq=23 |text=The O-erh-ch'i-ssu River begins in the southern section of the lofty A-erh-t'ai Mountains of Sinkiang. This river is over 2,900 kilometers long and has a large delta area rich in minerals such as gold, iron, copper, lead, zinc, mercury, mica, crystal and "ping-chou-shih" [3056 3166 4258 possibly cryolite]. At the '''source''' of the O-erh-ch'i-ssu River, the A-erh-t'ai Mountains reach more than 3,000 meters above sea level. The peaks of the mountains are covered with snow year-round, and rainfall is heavy in the summer. |translation={{lang|zh|我國新疆的額爾齊斯河,發源於巍峨的阿爾泰山東部,{{...}}

額爾齊斯河的發源地阿爾泰山,也是我國的名山,海拔三千米以上,山常年積雪,夏天雨水很多.}}}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-08-16|author=[http://www.theguardian.com/profile/johnvidal John Vidal] |volume=189|issue=10|page=8|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=[http://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2013/aug/10/china-india-water-grab-dams-himalayas-danger Dams endanger ecology of Himalayas] |passage=Most of the Himalayan rivers have been relatively untouched by dams near their '''sources'''.
